newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia Airline issuing jet fuel purchase tender.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Airline issuing jet fuel purchase tender.

text.p: Malaysia Airline System Bhd (MAS) is issuing a term tender to buy aviation jet fuel for one-or-two-year deliveries, industry sources said on Tuesday.

The tender, which is being issued during this week, is due to close on March 12 and offers will be valid until March 31. Sellers have to indicate their interest to take part in the tender by March 7, the sources said.

The tender calls for jet fuel supplies at 12 locations, totalling 36 million U.S. gallons, which does not include the airline homebase in Kuala Lumpur. The volume is slightly more than the last term contracts.
The locations include Australia, Dubai, Karachi, several locations in Southeast Asia, one location in Osaka, Japan and Buenos Aires in Argentina.

Japan Airlines (JAL) recently said that they plan to issue their tender in May based 100 percent on FEOP. Japan's All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) are using both FEOP and Platt's depending on the location and the seller.

Singapore Airlines recently awarded its 1997-1998 term tender for the Singapore portion at between three and five cents per gallon above prevailing Singapore spot quotes published by Platt's and FEOP.
This is the first time that SIA awarded some of its contract based in part on another publication apart from Platt's.
The tender is for one or two years, depending on the offers, and the jet fuel supplies are due to start from April.

The tender allows suppliers the option to offer cargoes based either on 50 percent of the Platt's publised price assessments and 50 percent on the Far East Oil Pricing (FEOP) quotations, or 100 percent Platt's, depending on the location.
So far three other airlines have been using FEOP for their jet fuel purchases, while one other Asian airline is using it on a trial basis.
SIA's contract for the Singapore portion is for the delivery of around 120 gallons, while the volume from 36 different locations worldwide sought another 260 million gallons.
